## Dr. Noopur Desai

Image: vet

Dr. Desai is a veterinary oncologist and surgeon working out of Mumbai and is a consulting veterinary radiation oncologist for various clinics in India. 
As a boarded Veterinary Oncologist, she is one of approximately 140 board- certified veterinary specialist in Radiation Oncology worldwide and the only Diplomate in Veterinary Oncology in India. Dr. Desai graduated as a veterinarian in 2008 following which she completed her MVSc (Masters) in Surgery from Mumbai. After working as a surgeon in India, she moved to the USA to pursue an International Scholar position in Medical Oncology from Michigan State University. She then went on to complete a residency in Radiation Oncology from University of Wisconsin- Madison and achieved Diplomate status from ACVR in Radiation Oncology. Before moving back to India, she worked as an Assistant Professor in Oncology at The Ohio State University- College of Veterinary Medicine.
Her interest is on the clinic floor treating patients, teaching newer generation of veterinarians, and performing clinical research. To further this passion of teaching and providing international quality care in veterinary oncology, Dr. Desai founded “The Cancer Vet” with a goal to providing world-class education in veterinary oncology in India.

## The licensed vets behind every consultation.
With Omelo Vet, you book a slot, describe your pet's concern, and a VCI-registered vet reviews it and speaks with you over video. It suits non-emergency issues, second opinions and follow-up care. For anything needing a physical exam or hands-on treatment, the vet will guide you to an in-person clinic.

Is an online vet consultation legal in India?

Yes. An online veterinary consultation is lawful in India when the person giving it is a veterinarian registered under the Indian Veterinary Council Act, 1984. The Act reserves veterinary practice to registered practitioners (sections 30(b) and 57(1)) and places no condition on the medium through which a registered practitioner gives advice. The Veterinary Council of India's Code of Ethics, 1992 contains no reference to remote or electronic consultation and imposes no physical-examination requirement. NITI Aayog observed in 2023 that India has no dedicated veterinary telemedicine framework, so there is no separate telemedicine licence, registration or approval to obtain. What makes an online vet consultation lawful in India is who gives it, not the medium. Every Omelo Vet consultation is with a veterinarian registered with a State Veterinary Council under that Act.

How does an online vet consultation work in India with Omelo?

It takes three steps. You book a consultation and enter your mobile number and your pet's concern. A licensed, VCI-registered vet reviews the details and connects with you on a video call at the slot you picked. During the call you get clear advice and next steps, and a written summary afterwards. Omelo Vet is available across India, 10am to 8pm IST Monday to Saturday, from ₹349.

How much does an online vet consultation cost in India?

An Omelo Vet online consultation starts at ₹349 (early-bird price, regularly ₹499) for a 15-minute video consultation with a licensed vet. It is one flat fee with no subscription and no hidden charges, and it is considerably cheaper than a typical in-clinic visit in most Indian cities.

Is Omelo an app or a website?

Our vets take video consultations from 10am to 8pm IST, Monday to Saturday, so Saturdays are covered. We do not currently run Sunday consultations. If your pet needs help outside those hours, go to a 24-hour emergency clinic.

Can a vet prescribe medicine over a video consultation in India?

Yes, within limits. Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 a registered veterinary practitioner counts as a registered medical practitioner for prescribing (rule 2(ee)(v)), and prescription-only medicines are dispensed against such a prescription written in the animal owner's name (rule 65(10)(b)). Nothing in those rules requires the consultation to have happened in person. What is not settled in India is whether an electronic prescription meets the signature requirement for veterinary use, so pharmacies differ in what they accept over the counter. On an Omelo Vet call the vet tells you what the likely problem is, which medicines are appropriate and which to avoid, and what dose is safe for your pet's species and weight, and you get that in a written summary afterwards. ## Your pet deserves expert guidance when it matters most.
